chapter_title: Measuring AI Capability: The METR Task-Horizon Studies
learning_objective: The learner will calculate the yearly AI inference cost per student from tokens per session, sessions per day, school days, and price per million tokens, to within one cent, in three of three challenges.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** ai-cost-per-student-calculator
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** calculate
**Learning Objective:** The learner will calculate the yearly AI inference cost per student from tokens per session, sessions per day, school days, and price per million tokens, to within one cent, in three of three challenges. **Template:** https://github.com/dmccreary/economics-course/tree/main/docs/sims/opportunity-cost-calculator
**Prerequisites:** AI inference cost, token, price per million tokens (all defined in the section "AI Inference Cost" above). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner commits answers to three challenges before the controls are unlocked. An answer is correct when it is within ±\$0.01 of the value in Content. Mastery is 3 of 3 correct. Using the controls afterward is exploration. **Misconceptions:** (1) Cost depends only on the number of sessions. (2) Cheaper models are always worse. (3) The cost of a capable AI tutor is out of reach for a public school. **Instructional Rationale:** Calculating cost from four inputs builds fluency with the units and makes the effect of a 280-fold price change tangible. Exploring afterward lets the learner see which input matters most. **Content:** The cost formula: cost per student per year = tokens per session × sessions per day × school days × price per million tokens ÷ 1,000,000. Inputs: | Input | Min | Max | Step | Default | Unit | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Tokens per session | 5,000 | 100,000 | 5,000 | 20,000 | tokens | | Sessions per school day | 1 | 5 | 1 | 1 | sessions | | School days per year | 150 | 200 | 10 | 180 | days | | Price per million tokens | 4 choices | | | \$0.07 | dollars | The four prices: \$20.00 (the November 2022 price for GPT-3.5-level performance as reported by the Stanford AI Index 2025), \$2.00 (illustrative), \$0.20 (illustrative), and \$0.07 (the October 2024 price as reported by the same source). Three challenges: | # | Tokens per session | Sessions per day | School days | Price per million | Correct cost per student per year | Working shown as feedback | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 20,000 | 1 | 180 | \$20.00 | \$72.00 | 20,000 × 1 × 180 = 3,600,000 tokens; 3.6 × \$20.00 = \$72.00. | | 2 | 20,000 | 1 | 180 | \$0.07 | \$0.25 | 3.6 million tokens × \$0.07 = \$0.252, which is about \$0.25. | | 3 | 40,000 | 2 | 180 | \$0.20 | \$2.88 | 40,000 × 2 × 180 = 14,400,000 tokens; 14.4 × \$0.20 = \$2.88. | **Provenance:** The two reported prices come from the Stanford AI Index 2025 as summarized in the chapter; the sim must show the source and label the \$2.00 and \$0.20 prices "Illustrative." The session sizes are illustrative, and the sim must say they apply to a GPT-3.5-level model. **Rules:** Annual tokens = tokens per session × sessions per day × school days. Cost = annual tokens ÷ 1,000,000 × price. Costs are shown to the cent, and to the tenth of a cent when under \$1 per student per year. A district total is shown for an enrollment of 12,000 students, which is the Chapter 1 example district. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner answers challenges 1, 2, and 3 as calculations and submits them. 2. The sim checks the answers and unlocks the controls. 3. The learner changes the inputs. The yearly cost, the daily cost, and the district total update at once. 4. The learner compares the cost at \$20.00 and at \$0.07 for the same usage. 5. The learner should notice that price per token changes the result far more than any realistic change in usage. **Feedback:** Three challenges, fixed order, two attempts each. Correct: "Correct: $[value]. [Working text]." Incorrect: "Not quite. Check the units: the price is per million tokens." After the second wrong attempt the value and working are shown. A score "n of 3" is shown. **Starting State:** Challenge 1 is shown with its inputs locked, and the prompt reads "What does one year of AI tutoring cost per student?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's worked example uses 20,000 tokens per session, one session per day, 180 days, 3.6 million tokens a year, prices of \$20.00 and \$0.07, costs of \$72.00 and about \$0.25, a 12,000-student district, and per-pupil spending of about \$15,600.
